# Replay

> Finds the turn your coding agent's prompt cache broke, what that turn cost, and what a
> different context layout would have saved. Runs entirely on your machine, reads transcripts
> already on disk, and needs no account.

Replay is a command-line tool and local proxy for people running coding agents (Claude Code,
Codex, Cursor, Grok, Ollama and others). When a prompt cache breaks, the provider re-bills the
whole conversation history at write prices. Nothing errors and nothing warns; the only trace is
a bill that looks like ordinary growth. Replay replays recorded sessions against the provider's
caching rules, turn by turn, and names the turn that broke.

It is deliberately narrower than a usage dashboard. `ccusage` and similar tools answer what you
spent. Replay answers which turn was billed twice and what changed on that turn to cause it.

## What makes it unusual

- **Every figure says how it was obtained.** Measured, estimated, or not measured — the tier is
  printed beside the number, and a screen that cannot measure says so rather than showing a
  plausible figure.
- **It retracts its own numbers in public.** A headline 98.8% was corrected to 4.2%. A sample
  described as 1,363 sessions was restated as 78. A quota measurement was published as a null
  result after the counter did not move across 3.09M tokens.
- **No dependencies.** `go.mod` is three lines with zero requires; there is no `go.sum` and no
  vendor directory.
- **No telemetry in the binary.** Two outbound calls exist and both are typed by the user.

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://redrobot.jp/replay.sh | sh
```

The installer is written to be read before it is run. `--dry-run` prints what it would do.
